heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional-grade visual content creation. Generate images, edit visuals, and produce synchronized video with audio using advanced multimodal AI.
heroStrategy.designNote: Hero uses an unexpected enterprise-launch treatment: left-aligned copy on a rich orange-to-charcoal mesh with a full-bleed autoplay loop video embedded as a layered right-side media panel. The video should feel premium and abstract rather than literal—AI-generated motion, output previews, and UI-shell framing. Use large dramatic typography (H1 64px+; H2 40px+ elsewhere), rounded orange CTA, and subtle grid/orb decorations to reinforce the high-precision AI brand. Keep the hero immersive, production-ready, and conversion-focused with strong logo proof directly beneath the headline.

repetitionBreakers: Start with an immersive orange-led hero, then switch immediately to a logos-first trust bar.
Use a tabs-with-preview product module so the two product sections feel like one interactive capability journey instead of stacked repeat cards.
Alternate surfaces between white, light gray, and white again to prevent visual monotony.
Make testimonials a compact spotlight grid, then end with a centered lead capture card to sharpen the close.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 for high-quality AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for AI video creation. Built for marketing, design, and video teams that need premium visual content fast.

sections.backgroundTreatment: video-led gradient field with layered AI motion shells, subtle grain, and a darkened media panel on the right
sections.designNote: PrimaryGoal: convert warm traffic by matching the ad promise immediately. NarrativeMode: product-led launch. TrustStrategy: continuity first, with a light logo hint only if space allows. VisualDominance: hero-product, so the right side should show dynamic AI-generated imagery/video UI rather than a static illustration. CTA aggression is moderate: one dominant orange full-width-on-mobile button labeled 'Get started'. The headline must answer what this is; the subheadline must answer who it is for. Keep copy compact and premium.

TrustStrategy: logos-first, but because explicit customer logos are not provided, use a clean static logo grid only if real recognisable logos can be inserted; otherwise replace with a narrow metric strip. This section should appear early, immediately after hero, and feel lighter than the hero. Keep it horizontally compact and authoritative, not promotional.

Use one interactive tabbed module with a preview panel to separate the two product lines. Open on Seedream 4.5 because it has more features and is the primary click driver for image-generation intent. Show Seedream as the first tab with a polished visual preview and concise feature bullets focused on text-image alignment, high-resolution output, typographic rendering, and multi-image composition. When the user switches to Seedance 1.5 Pro, shift the preview to motion/video frames and compress the copy into capability-led points. This section must feel high-density but not crowded, with strong visual contrast against the hero. Avoid a flat static grid because there are 5+ features.

If included, make this a short utility reassurance band rather than a generic vendor pitch. Use 3 concise proof points only, in icon-list format, with a restrained card rhythm. Keep it visually lighter than the product area and avoid duplicating claims already made in product sections.

Treat pricing as a decision-support block, not a hard sell. Show two side-by-side cards with the image model as the default visual emphasis and the video model as the premium option. Include the specified pricing details without adding extra plan noise. Keep both cards equal in structure but vary emphasis using outline, iconography, and feature density. CTA must remain exactly 'Get started' on every button, styled with solid accent orange at 100% opacity. This section should feel more transactional than the rest, increasing conversion pressure without becoming aggressive.

Use a 3-card testimonial grid with compact, high-trust quotes. Since there are 5 testimonials, surface the strongest 3 in the main view and use a subtle 'more voices' expansion if needed. Choose quotes that reinforce speed, multimodal quality, and demo usefulness. This should read as credibility after pricing, not as a standalone social wall.

End with a centered lead-capture card that feels like the cleanest conversion moment on the page. Since the user journey is warm and the CTA should favor seeing it in action, the form should be minimal, with one dominant button labeled 'Get started' in solid orange. Keep it visually calm, with generous white space and a premium shadow so it closes the page decisively.

If a news/media or logo strip is used, keep it static and low-height, never marquee. Because explicit media logos are not supplied, do not force this section unless you can populate it with real recognisable proof. Otherwise omit this block entirely. If present, use it as a quiet credibility footer rather than a promotional banner.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium enterprise AI marketplace with a confident orange identity, video-first storytelling, and strong trust-led structure. The page should feel like a high-end launch for creative teams: bold hero, dominant logo proof, clean capability bands, and clear conversion paths without clutter.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic video background in the hero with abstract AI-generated visuals, motion blur, and layered UI shells. Support sections should use polished product mockups, model capability cards, and small SVG icons rather than dense imagery. Show logo-proof as a prominent static strip near the top and, if real logos are available, again near the pricing area.

PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width promotional hero with brand/logo lockup, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and compact benefit list; left-aligned content in a two-column grid with strong visual hierarchy and a CTA-led conversion focus.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single dominant hero followed by a conversion form block and then stacked product/feature sections; content progresses from broad value proposition to more detailed capability proof, with clear vertical separation and repeated section framing.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Structured white content cards/blocks with minimal ornamentation, strong typography, and list-based feature presentation; emphasis is on clarity and scannability rather than decorative depth.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion CTA in the hero, with secondary conversion intent implied by a later form-driven CTA block; product sections use section-level CTAs only where needed, favoring lead capture and request-demo actions over repeated button clusters.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module present; the page is positioned as enterprise/lead-generation rather than transactional pricing.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not present in the provided reference fragment; likely minimal or deferred below the visible fold.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Image-led brand/hero area with lightweight logo presence; no heavy media gallery, instead relying on text hierarchy, icon bullets, and form content for engagement.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with label-headline-description structure followed by a compact feature list; each section is self-contained, uses progressive disclosure, and supports comparison by repeating the same pattern for multiple products.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block directly after the hero with a titled card container and hidden tracking inputs; form is visually separated from marketing content and designed as a conversion checkpoint.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-first presentation with no visible motion system in the reference fragment; interaction appears functional rather than animated.

designStrategy.reasoning: This is a lead-generation landing page for solution-aware professionals evaluating ByteDance generative AI models, so the page should lead with product clarity, strong proof, and an enterprise-style request/demo flow rather than transactional purchase intent. Because the audience trusts recognizable brands most, logos should be the dominant trust element near the top and repeated through the page. The hero should be immersive with video background, but still message-led so the value proposition is instantly clear. Since the content is long and includes two distinct products, the layout should remain balanced and highly scannable with clear section separation, stacked feature blocks, and a visible conversion path throughout.
